name: evaluation of generative drug discovery
description: "How to evaluate the de novo designs proposed by a generative model?" Despite the transformative potential of generative deep learning in drug discovery, this seemingly simple question has no clear answer. The absence of standardized guidelines challenges both the benchmarking of generative approaches and the selection of molecules for prospective studies. In this work, we take a fresh - critical and constructive - perspective on de novo design evaluation. By training chemical language models, we analyze approximately 1 billion molecule designs and discover principles consistent across different neural networks and datasets. We uncover a key confounder: the size of the generated molecular library significantly impacts evaluation outcomes, often leading to misleading model comparisons. We find increasing the number of designs as a remedy and propose new and compute-efficient metrics to compute at large-scale. We also identify critical pitfalls in commonly used metrics - such as uniquene
reputation: A methodological benchmark paper rather than a single fixed leaderboard, with influence mainly in generative chemistry evaluation discussions.
notes: Evaluation is highly sensitive to library size and metric choice; not a single standardized benchmark with a fixed leaderboard, and comparisons can be misleading without controlling for sampling budget.
